# Admission Functions

Reusable functions for preparing a candidate process document and admitting parties needed by its host. They distinguish admission approval, each proposed party’s consent, access readiness, roster installation and source linking. Functions act when invoked; the definition does not establish an automatic trigger.

## Context and candidate staging

The runtime constant `clauseKey` selects `/process_<clauseKey>`, whose `entries` hold preparation items and whose `admission` contains `ledger`, `grants` and `retired` records. Paths refer to the document executing these functions, including when that document is nested. Paths inspected inside `candidate` or source objects belong to those objects.

`candidateStage(checked)` consumes `checked.item`, `checked.candidate` and `checked.origin`, and returns an updated item. It preserves an established `candidateOrigin`, rejecting a different origin with `PREPARATION_CANDIDATE_REPLACEMENT_FORBIDDEN`, while updating `candidateRef` to the supplied publication’s reference.

Host admission is considered when any `bindings.sources` value is `self`. The function identifies candidate parties not covered by `/activation/parties`. Coverage ignores role names: it matches `lead.channel` identity and requires nonempty `readerKeys` with equal lengths and matching membership. A missing party keeps its candidate role unless that role is already occupied; then a `participant_` name derived from its lead channel is used.

Missing parties require a nonempty `/clauses/activation/parameters/admission/approvers` list. `candidatePartyAccessDocuments` selects access documents from the candidate’s `/activation/accessPaths` by matching `allowedTimelines` against party transport timelines. It retains one document per role, with later matches replacing earlier ones, then delegates validation to `requirePartyAccessDocuments`.

The resulting `admissionToken` captures:

- `parties`: the missing host parties, and `accessDocuments`: their selected access evidence.
- `accessScope`: the combined host roster, host `readers` and host `processOrigin`.
- `activationRevision`: the host revision being reviewed.
- `candidateOrigin`, `itemPath` and `requirementRef`: the candidate identity and preparation-item references.
- `attempt`: the item’s `admissionAttempt`, defaulting to `0`.

`admissionRef` identifies this complete token. An existing token must match; otherwise staging rejects with `ADMISSION_REAPPROVAL_REQUIRED`. The returned status is `admission_pending`, preserving `consents` or defaulting them to `{}`.

When no host parties are missing, staging returns `awaiting_activation` unless the candidate’s `/activation/active` is explicitly `true`. It then checks every declared document source for initialization, the required process origin, roster coverage and active status. An origin mismatch rejects; other unmet checks produce `linking`. Passing these checks produces `ready`. This staging check does not include the additional `selectionPath` check used by inherited `namedSourcesReady`.

## Approval, consent and installation

`nextAdmissionRequest()` first retires an invalid pending admission. It returns no new request while `/admission/ledger/proposal/id` exists. Otherwise, a pending item without a grant produces `ready: true` and a proposal request containing `proposalId: admissionRef`, the ledger’s `expectedRevision`, the grants `path`, a `replacement` preserving existing grants and adding the token, and `preservePending: true`. Returning this request does not record or approve the proposal.

`admissionInstallRequest()` considers pending items only when `/admission/ledger/history/<admissionRef>` is explicitly `true` and `/admission/grants/<admissionRef>` equals the item’s token. These are separate prerequisites from party consent and access readiness.

`installAdmissionConsentOperations(item)` requires a token and a successful `accessValid` check for the combined roster, host readers and host access paths. It installs an admission-specific channel from each proposed party’s `lead.channel` and a corresponding `consentAdmission_…` operation under `/contracts`. Existing declarations must match exactly; conflicting channels or operations reject. Each operation accepts text `admissionRef` and `decision`, restricted to `approve` or `decline`, and forwards `call/request` to `recordConsent` with fixed `itemPath`, `admissionRef` and `party` constants. The supplied evidence does not define `recordConsent`’s further acceptance rules.

Every role in the token’s `parties` must have `consents/<role>` equal to `approve`. Missing consent is not approval. A `decline` makes the item `admission_denied` and emits `Document Admission Progress`.

For a token matching `/activation/revision`, the first installation check without a matching `accessRequested` marker records that marker and emits an access request carrying `accessDocuments`, `parties`, `admissionRef`, `expectedRevision`, `clauseKey` and `itemPath`. This can precede unanimous consent. The marker records a request, not completed access. The call returns `ready: false` after issuing it.

Once all proposed parties approve, the token revision remains current and combined-roster access passes `accessValid`, the function changes the item to `installing` and returns `ready: true`, `itemPath` and an installation `request` containing `admissionRef`, `expectedRevision` and `parties`. The detailed access-validation rules are delegated and are not supplied here.

The inherited `admitApprovedParties(input)` performs roster installation. It rejects frozen parties, a stale `expectedRevision`, an absent admission policy, invalid party names, failed main-party identity checks, insufficient access and conflicting contract names. Existing roles must represent the same main party and retain their existing data; new roles are added. An unchanged roster returns `outcome: duplicate`. A changed roster installs party channels and handlers, increments the activation revision, commits activation state and emits `Participants admitted` events for the supplied additions. It leaves `required` unchanged.

`finishAdmission(input)` requires `input.itemPath` to identify an `installing` item and verifies that the host roster covers the token’s parties through matching lead channels and `requireSameMainParty`. It records the current activation revision as `admittedRevision`, changes the item to `linking`, emits progress with `status: admitted`, and returns `outcome: acceptedNew`. This confirms the roster-coverage completion step; candidate readiness still depends on activation and linking.

## Retirement and reapproval

`retireInvalidAdmission()` examines pending items. Any recorded `decline` takes precedence over a stale activation revision for that item. It retires one qualifying item per call as `admission_denied` or `reapproval_required`.

`retireAdmission(item, reason)` records the status and archives `token`, `consents` and `reason` under `/admission/retired/<admissionRef>`. If the ledger’s pending proposal has that reference, it clears the proposal and increments the ledger revision. It emits `Document Admission Progress`; it does not remove existing grants or history.

`rebaseAdmission(input)` requires `call/requireExactDocumentVersion: true` and a `call/channel` listed in the host’s admission `approvers`. `input.key` defaults to `single` and selects the entry indexed by that key’s content identity. `input.admissionRef` must identify the admission requiring reapproval. Repeating `lastRebasedAdmissionRef` returns `duplicate`; another stale reference or an inappropriate status rejects.

A successful rebase removes `admissionToken`, `admissionRef` and `consents`, increments `admissionAttempt` from a default of `0`, records `lastRebasedAdmissionRef`, and sets `awaiting_provider`. Its progress event reports `reprovision_required` and `supersededAdmissionRef`. Other item fields, including the candidate origin, remain. `rebaseAdmissionPublic` forwards the request after removing its `type` field.

Activation revision, admission-ledger revision and admission attempt are distinct counters. Missing entry collections are processed as empty, but no default item status or revision is established. A helper’s `ready: false` means it returned no next request or installation; the same call may have recorded progress or emitted an access request.

## Inherited document and activation behavior

Factory functions use `bindings.collection` for creation destinations, `bindings.parties` for explicit child-party mappings, `bindings.sources` for named source mappings and `bindings.template` for a bound template path. `configuredTemplate` prefers configuration `parameters.template`, otherwise the connection snapshot’s `template`. Connection configuration and snapshots are supplied through their respective functions.

`checkCreation(input)` requires a nonempty text `key` containing neither `/` nor `~`. Its creation intent captures the template, party mappings, inherited channels, source paths, `fields`, `values` and `requestId`; `fields` and `values` default to `{}`, and `requestId` defaults to `key`. An occupied destination is a duplicate only when its `creationIntent` matches; otherwise it rejects with `DOCUMENT_KEY_CONFLICT`.

`constructDocument` requires an uninitialized template. Explicit party mappings use `prepareChild`, which requires an Activation clause and delegates mapping resolution. Without mappings, legacy `activateChild` uses configured `parties`, or all host parties when that list is empty, and configured `readers`, defaulting to none. It returns the child unchanged if the host has no activation state. Child preparation copies host access references and checks channel conflicts.

`inheritChannels` permits only supported explicit participant channels. `fields` must be allowlisted and nonreserved; `values` use configured `fieldPaths`, require existing constraint slots and reject reserved runtime paths. Legacy `sourcePaths` must reference initialized documents. Construction records `creationIntent`, assigns `instanceKey`, and can assign identities to uninitialized `identityChildren`. `create` stores the constructed child and emits `Document Started`; this does not establish activation or admission completion.

`configureSources` adds document-access registration and, when configured, named-source requirements. Named mappings cannot coexist with legacy `sourcePaths`; they must cover declared aliases and identify active initialized processes. `self` refers to the executing host and records the child’s selection path. Reserved clause names reject. The shown `configuredSources` and `sourceDeclarationMatches` implementations reject with `SOURCE_VALIDATOR_NOT_COMPILED` until specialized implementations are supplied.

`bindSource` accepts a declared `alias` and either `document` or a nonempty `sourcePath`, with `sourcePath` taking precedence. It verifies origin, active status and host-party coverage before storing a source reference. `processOrigin` identifies `/contracts/initialized/document`, whose absence rejects. Existing bindings cannot change origin. `namedSourcesReady` additionally checks a nonempty `selectionPath` for an initialized selection pointing back to the executing process; `refreshSourceReadiness` records the result at `/sourceLinks/ready`. Source binding does not grant commercial approval.

Inherited activation approval requires exact-document review, a party channel, the current `revision` and valid access. When negotiation has `allowedPaths`, `termsRef` is required; any supplied reference must match `/activation/terms/ref`. Party management also requires exact review and an unfrozen roster. A lead can replace its own party or add a party when `allowNewParties` permits it. Replacement requires `lead.channel`; successful management clears approvals, increments the revision and adds a new role to `required`. Guards default missing `frozen` and `allowNewParties` to `false`.

Activation derives `accessReady` and `functional` from access checks, including current-revision pending access additions. `termsAccepted` requires approvals for every `required` role and a successful `termsCurrent` check. `active` additionally requires that the process is not closed. Derived statuses distinguish `WAITING_FOR_ACCESS`, `SUSPENDED_ACCESS`, `AWAITING_ACCEPTANCE`, `ACTIVE` and `CLOSED`. Committing roster or required-party changes can revise existing terms, retire a negotiation proposal and clear approvals when negotiation is enabled. Admission therefore does not independently guarantee continued activation.

`registerDocumentAccessPublic` accepts `documents` containing one to sixteen Timeline Access publications. Registration requires exact-document review and a party-lead channel before delegating to `installTimelineAccess`; its detailed installation rules are not supplied. Callable operations remain subject to their established channels and guards and do not establish a particular reader’s permission or obligation.
